I've updated `meter.c` for SDK 89.0, but I haven't compiled it. There's no SDK toolchain here, and my first attempt to run a script was denied, so I made the changes with direct edits.

## What will break (SDK 88.2 → 89.0)

1. **`furi_hal_adc_configure` has a new signature.**
   - It now takes a second argument, `FuriHalAdcScale`, so the old one-argument call would not compile.
   - I changed the call to `furi_hal_adc_configure(meter.adc, FuriHalAdcScale2048)`.
   - **Needs your check:** the tables don't list the enum values, so `FuriHalAdcScale2048` is my guess. I left a TODO. Confirm the name and pick the scale that suits your voltage range.
2. **`meter_legacy_format` is no longer in the 89.0 table.**
   - Its status went from `+` to `-`, so the app would fail at link time or load time.
   - I replaced the call with `snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%.*f", (int)meter_default_precision, (double)meter.volts)`. That keeps its precision behaviour, since `meter_default_precision` is still exported.
   - I swapped the hand-written prototype for an `extern const uint8_t meter_default_precision;` declaration. Drop that line if the SDK headers already declare it.
3. **`cfw_meter_set_backlight_boost` is not in either SDK table.**
   - It comes from `meter_extra.h`, which was copied from a community firmware fork. It exists only on that fork, so the app would not load on stock firmware, and probably not on 89.0 of the fork either.
   - I removed the call and the `#include "meter_extra.h"`. I left `meter_extra.h` itself in the folder.
   - The backlight boost is gone from the app. If you need it, keep it behind a build flag for that fork only.

## Not affected
- `furi_hal_adc_acquire`, `furi_hal_adc_read`, `furi_hal_adc_convert_to_voltage`, `furi_hal_adc_release`, and the three timer functions are unchanged.
- `meter_default_precision` is unchanged.
- The new `furi_hal_adc_set_averaging` is optional and the app doesn't need it.
- `internal_adc_calibrate` is private (`-`) in both versions, and the app doesn't use it.

## Separate issue I noticed
`furi_timer_free` is called while the timer may still be running. Calling `furi_timer_stop` first would be safer. I didn't change it because it isn't part of the migration.
